properties.natural_language: Before Check Execution Result can execute, the system must be in Transaction Execution Complete.
After Check Execution Result completes, the system must transition to Execution Succeeded with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Execution Result completes, the system must transition to Execution Failed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Set Status Code to 1 can execute, the system must be in Execution Succeeded.
Before Set Status Code to 0 can execute, the system must be in Execution Failed.
After Set Status Code to 1 completes, the system must transition to Receipt Created with Status with all state invariants preserved.
After Set Status Code to 0 completes, the system must transition to Receipt Created with Status with all state invariants preserved.
Before Store Receipt in Block can execute, the system must be in Receipt Created with Status.
After Store Receipt in Block completes, the system must transition to Receipt Finalized in Block with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Block Height vs Byzantium can execute, the system must be in Pre-Byzantium Receipt Format.
After Check Block Height vs Byzantium completes, the system must transition to Below Byzantium Fork Block with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Block Height vs Byzantium completes, the system must transition to At or Above Byzantium Fork with all state invariants preserved.

Before Use New Receipt Format can execute, the system must be in At or Above Byzantium Fork.
After Use New Receipt Format completes, the system must transition to Post-Byzantium Receipt Format with all state invariants preserved.

After Retrieve Receipt from Chain completes, the system must transition to Receipt Retrieved with all state invariants preserved.

After Check Status Code Field completes, the system must transition to Status Code is 0 with all state invariants preserved.
Before Handle Successful Transaction can execute, the system must be in Status Code is 1.
Before Handle Failed Transaction can execute, the system must be in Status Code is 0.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP658-01): The specification states 'any operation that causes the transaction or top-level call to revert' triggers status 0, but does not explicitly define all revert conditions. — the system must enforce: Assume revert conditions include: REVERT opcode, out-of-gas, invalid opcode, stack underflow/overflow, and any other EVM exception.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP658-02): The exact byte position and encoding of the status field within the RLP-encoded receipt is not specified. — the system must enforce: Assume status replaces state root at the same position in the RLP structure, as a single byte (0x00 or 0x01).

The system assumes: Block producers correctly set the status code based on actual execution outcome.. If violated: Incorrect status codes could cause applications to incorrectly interpret transaction outcomes, leading to financial losses.

The system assumes: The intermediate state root was already unused due to EIP-98, so removing it has no practical impact.. If violated: If any tooling or contracts relied on the state root, they would break at the Byzantium fork.

The system assumes: All clients and tooling will be updated to interpret the new receipt format correctly.. If violated: Tools expecting the old format might misparse receipts, leading to incorrect transaction status reporting.
Before Get Safe Beacon Block Root can execute, the system must be in Justified Checkpoint Available in Store.
After Get Safe Beacon Block Root completes, the system must transition to Safe Beacon Block Root Determined with all state invariants preserved.
Before Get Safe Execution Block Hash can execute, the system must be in Safe Beacon Block Root Determined.
After Get Safe Execution Block Hash completes, the system must transition to Safe Execution Block Hash Returned with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Block Epoch >= BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH can execute, the system must be in Safe Beacon Block Retrieved from Store.
After Check Block Epoch >= BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH completes, the system must transition to Block is Pre-Bellatrix (No Execution Payload) with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Block Epoch >= BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH completes, the system must transition to Block is Post-Bellatrix (Has Execution Payload) with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-SAFEBLOCK-01): The get_safe_beacon_block_root function 'is meant to be improved in the future' using the justified checkpoint as 'a stopgap'. — the system must enforce: Assume the current justified-checkpoint-based implementation is the authoritative behavior for all deployed versions. Future improvements are out of scope. This is an assumption.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-SAFEBLOCK-02): Safe from reorganization under 'honest majority and certain network synchronicity assumptions' without specifying exact synchronicity bounds. — the system must enforce: Assume standard Ethereum synchronicity model: messages delivered within a known bounded delay. The exact bound is protocol-version-specific. This is an assumption.

The system assumes: The justified checkpoint in the store is accurate and was produced by an honest supermajority of validators.. If violated: If the justified checkpoint is based on a dishonest supermajority attestation, the 'safe' block may actually be on a fork that gets reorganized, misleading execution layer clients.

The system assumes: The beacon block store always contains the block referenced by the justified checkpoint root.. If violated: A missing block would cause get_safe_execution_block_hash to fail, potentially returning a stale or incorrect safe head to the execution layer.

All data received via User submits EIP-1559 transaction from EXT-USER-DAPP-TYPE1 must be validated before processing. Conversion must correctly map gas_price to both max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas. Access list must be preserved unchanged. Chain ID must be maintained. Type field updated from 0x1 to 0x2. Incorrect conversion could alter transaction economics.
If input from EXT-USER-DAPP-TYPE1 via User submits EIP-1559 transaction fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Validate Transaction Format can execute, the system must be in Type-2 Transaction Submitted.
After Validate Transaction Format completes, the system must transition to Transaction Format Valid with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Max Fee Against Base Fee can execute, the system must be in Transaction Format Valid.
After Check Max Fee Against Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Max Fee Sufficient with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Max Fee Against Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Max Fee Insufficient with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Sender Balance can execute, the system must be in Max Fee Sufficient.
After Check Sender Balance completes, the system must transition to Balance Sufficient with all state invariants preserved.
After Balance Sufficient completes, Transaction in Mempool must proceed as specified by: Accept to mempool.
Before Compute Effective Gas Price can execute, the system must be in Transaction in Mempool.
After Compute Effective Gas Price completes, the system must transition to Transaction Included in Block with all state invariants preserved.
Before Read Parent Block Values can execute, the system must be in Parent Block Known.
After Read Parent Block Values completes, the system must transition to Parent Values Loaded with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compare Gas Used to Target can execute, the system must be in Parent Values Loaded.
After Compare Gas Used to Target completes, the system must transition to Gas Used at Target with all state invariants preserved.
After Compare Gas Used to Target completes, the system must transition to Gas Used Above Target with all state invariants preserved.
After Compare Gas Used to Target completes, the system must transition to Gas Used Below Target with all state invariants preserved.
Before Keep Base Fee Unchanged can execute, the system must be in Gas Used at Target.
Before Increase Base Fee can execute, the system must be in Gas Used Above Target.
Before Decrease Base Fee can execute, the system must be in Gas Used Below Target.
After Keep Base Fee Unchanged completes, the system must transition to New Base Fee Calculated with all state invariants preserved.
After Increase Base Fee completes, the system must transition to New Base Fee Calculated with all state invariants preserved.
After Decrease Base Fee completes, the system must transition to New Base Fee Calculated with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Gas Limit Change can execute, the system must be in New Block Received.
After Validate Gas Limit Change completes, the system must transition to Gas Limit Valid with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Gas Limit Change completes, the system must transition to Gas Limit Invalid with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Minimum Gas Limit can execute, the system must be in Gas Limit Valid.
After Validate Minimum Gas Limit completes, the system must transition to Minimum Gas Satisfied with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Block Base Fee can execute, the system must be in Minimum Gas Satisfied.
After Validate Block Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Base Fee Matches Calculation with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Block Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Base Fee Mismatch with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Gas Used can execute, the system must be in Base Fee Matches Calculation.
After Validate Gas Used completes, the system must transition to Gas Used Within Limit with all state invariants preserved.
After Gas Used Within Limit completes, Block Passes EIP-1559 Validation must proceed as specified by: All checks pass.
After Gas Limit Invalid completes, Block Fails Validation must proceed as specified by: Reject block.
After Base Fee Mismatch completes, Block Fails Validation must proceed as specified by: Reject block.
Before Calculate Fee Components can execute, the system must be in Transaction Executing.
After Calculate Fee Components completes, the system must transition to Fee Components Calculated with all state invariants preserved.
Before Burn Base Fee can execute, the system must be in Fee Components Calculated.
After Burn Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Base Fee Burned with all state invariants preserved.
Before Pay Priority Fee to Validator can execute, the system must be in Base Fee Burned.
After Pay Priority Fee to Validator completes, the system must transition to Priority Fee Paid with all state invariants preserved.
Before Refund Unused Gas can execute, the system must be in Priority Fee Paid.
After Refund Unused Gas completes, the system must transition to Transaction Fee Settlement Complete with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1559-01): The specification lacks explicit rules for transaction pool (mempool) behavior and eviction policies for EIP-1559 transactions. — the system must enforce: Assume mempool implementations use priority_fee_per_gas for sorting and evict transactions whose max_fee_per_gas falls below projected base fees.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1559-02): The phrase 'gas limit changes must stay within ±0.1% of parent block' does not specify whether this is per-block or cumulative. — the system must enforce: Assume this is a per-block constraint: each block's gas limit can differ from its parent by at most ±0.1% (actually 1/1024 ≈ 0.098%).

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1559-03): The initial base fee of 1 Gwei is specified for the London fork but behavior for new chains or reorgs past London is unclear. — the system must enforce: Assume INITIAL_BASE_FEE = 1 Gwei applies only to the first EIP-1559 block, and subsequent blocks always calculate from parent.

The system assumes: Block producers will include transactions honestly based on priority fee rather than engaging in base fee manipulation strategies.. If violated: Validators could collude to keep blocks artificially small, preventing base fee from decreasing, extracting more MEV from users.

The system assumes: An attacker cannot sustain blocks that are consistently 100% full (2x target) for extended periods without significant cost.. If violated: Sustained full blocks would cause base fee to increase by ~12.5% per block, potentially reaching extreme levels and causing network instability.

The system assumes: Wallet software and user interfaces will correctly implement max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas estimation.. If violated: Users may overpay significantly if max_fee is set too high, or have transactions stuck if set too low during fee spikes.

The system assumes: The deflationary pressure from burning base fees will not cause economic instability or hoarding behavior.. If violated: ETH could become overly deflationary during high-usage periods, potentially destabilizing the economic model.
Before Extract Execution Payload Data can execute, the system must be in Beacon Block Finalized.
After Extract Execution Payload Data completes, Build Light Client Header with Blob Gas must proceed as specified by: Construct header with Deneb fields.
After Build Light Client Header with Blob Gas completes, the system must transition to Light Client Header Ready with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Block Epoch Against DENEB_FORK_EPOCH can execute, the system must be in Block Selected for Light Client Header.
After Check Block Epoch Against DENEB_FORK_EPOCH completes, the system must transition to Pre-Deneb Header Format with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Block Epoch Against DENEB_FORK_EPOCH completes, the system must transition to Deneb Header Format with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-DENEB-LC-FN-01): The specification does not describe what happens if a light client receives a Deneb-format header but expects a pre-Deneb format. — the system must enforce: Assume that light clients must be upgraded to understand Deneb headers after the fork epoch. The P2P interface layer handles fork-specific deserialization.

The system assumes: Full nodes honestly populate the blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas fields in light client headers from the actual execution payload.. If violated: Light clients could receive manipulated blob gas data, leading to incorrect fee estimation or misjudgment of network blob utilization.

The system assumes: The Deneb fork epoch is configured identically across all nodes in the network.. If violated: Mismatched fork epochs would cause some nodes to include blob gas fields while others don't, breaking light client sync across the fork boundary.
Before Compute Fork Version for Epoch can execute, the system must be in Current Epoch Known.
After Compute Fork Version for Epoch completes, the system must transition to Active Fork Version Determined with all state invariants preserved.
Before Derive Fork Digest can execute, the system must be in Active Fork Version Determined.
After Derive Fork Digest completes, the system must transition to P2P Gossip Topics Active with all state invariants preserved.
Before Verify Peer Fork Digest Compatibility can execute, the system must be in Peer Connection Requested.
After Verify Peer Fork Digest Compatibility completes, the system must transition to Peer Fork Digest Compatible with all state invariants preserved.
After Verify Peer Fork Digest Compatibility completes, the system must transition to Peer Fork Digest Incompatible with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP6800-P2P-01): The P2P interface page provides only the compute_fork_version helper but does not detail specific gossip topics, request/response protocols, or message formats for EIP-6800. — the system must enforce: Assume EIP-6800 inherits the standard Ethereum consensus P2P protocol (gossipsub topics, req/resp protocols) with only the fork version changed. Specific Verkle-tree-related messages may be defined elsewhere. This is an assumption.

The system assumes: Peers transition to the EIP-6800 fork version at the correct epoch, maintaining network connectivity during the transition.. If violated: Peers stuck on a pre-EIP6800 fork version would be unable to communicate with upgraded peers, causing network partitioning.

The system assumes: The fork version ordering in compute_fork_version is evaluated in descending order (newest first), ensuring the correct version is always selected.. If violated: If evaluation order is incorrect, a node might select an older fork version and be isolated from upgraded peers.
Before Check Fork Activation Condition can execute, the system must be in Electra State Active.
After Check Fork Activation Condition completes, the system must transition to Electra State Active with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Fork Activation Condition completes, Execute upgrade_to_fulu() must proceed as specified by: Epoch == FULU_FORK_EPOCH.
After Execute upgrade_to_fulu() completes, Update Fork Version Fields must proceed as specified by: Update fork metadata.
After Update Fork Version Fields completes, Initialize Proposer Lookahead must proceed as specified by: Initialize new Fulu state field.
After Initialize Proposer Lookahead completes, the system must transition to Fulu State Active with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compute Lookahead Epoch Range can execute, the system must be in Proposer Lookahead Uninitialized.
After Compute Lookahead Epoch Range completes, Get Beacon Proposer Indices Per Slot must proceed as specified by: Iterate through slots.
After Get Beacon Proposer Indices Per Slot completes, the system must transition to Proposer Lookahead Populated with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Epoch Boundary Alignment can execute, the system must be in Pre-Fork Electra State.
After Validate Epoch Boundary Alignment completes, Verify State Field Preservation must proceed as specified by: Boundary valid, check state integrity.
After Verify State Field Preservation completes, the system must transition to Post-Fork State Validated with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Epoch Boundary Alignment completes, the system must transition to Fork Transition Rejected with all state invariants preserved.
After Verify State Field Preservation completes, the system must transition to Fork Transition Rejected with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-FULU-FORK-01): No specification of behavior if a node misses the fork epoch and syncs past it — the system must enforce: Assume nodes syncing past the fork epoch apply upgrade_to_fulu retroactively during state replay at the correct epoch boundary. This is an assumption.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-FULU-FORK-02): For genesis networks, the upgrade function 'applies directly to the genesis state' without specifying how fork.previous_version is handled — the system must enforce: Assume fork.previous_version is set to FULU_FORK_VERSION itself (same as current_version) for genesis networks, as there is no prior fork. This is an assumption.

The system assumes: All nodes in the network agree on FULU_FORK_EPOCH = 411392 and activate simultaneously. If violated: Network split if some nodes fork at different epochs, creating two incompatible chains

The system assumes: The proposer lookahead initialization at fork time is deterministic and produces identical results on all nodes. If violated: Nodes would disagree on proposer assignments post-fork, causing missed slots and attestation failures
Before Calculate Excess Blob Gas can execute, the system must be in Blob Schedule Loaded from Config.
Before Calculate Excess Blob Gas can execute, the system must be in Parent Block Header Available.
After Calculate Excess Blob Gas completes, the system must transition to Excess Blob Gas Value Computed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Calculate Base Fee Per Blob Gas can execute, the system must be in Excess Blob Gas Value Computed.
After Calculate Base Fee Per Blob Gas completes, the system must transition to Blob Base Fee Determined with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check EL Fork Activation Timestamp can execute, the system must be in Pre-BPO Fork Active Parameters.
Before Check CL Fork Activation Epoch can execute, the system must be in Pre-BPO Fork Active Parameters.
After Check EL Fork Activation Timestamp completes, Switch to New Blob Parameters must proceed as specified by: Timestamp condition met.
After Check CL Fork Activation Epoch completes, Switch to New Blob Parameters must proceed as specified by: Epoch condition met.
After Switch to New Blob Parameters completes, the system must transition to Post-BPO Fork Active Parameters with all state invariants preserved.
Before Rotate Fork Digest Value can execute, the system must be in ENR Next Fork Digest Set.
After Rotate Fork Digest Value completes, the system must transition to Gossip Topics Using New Fork Digest with all state invariants preserved.
After Rotate Fork Digest Value completes, the system must transition to Peer Discovery ENR Updated with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7892-01): No security risks have been identified. — the system must enforce: Assume this applies only to the parameter-change mechanism itself and does not cover risks from specific parameter values (e.g., setting max too high). This is an assumption.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7892-02): The specification does not define behavior when EL and CL blob schedules are misaligned. — the system must enforce: Assume misaligned schedules constitute a configuration error that clients should detect at startup. This is an assumption.

The system assumes: EL and CL blob schedules are always configured consistently, with EL max matching CL MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK and EL timestamps aligning with CL epoch boundaries.. If violated: Inconsistent blob limits between layers could cause valid CL blocks to fail EL validation or vice versa, leading to chain splits or stuck finality.

The system assumes: All nodes on the network upgrade their blobSchedule configuration before the activation timestamp/epoch.. If violated: Nodes with stale configuration would reject blocks with the new blob parameters, causing network partitions.
Data from external entity EXT-WALLET via User creates transaction must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Prepare Signing Data can execute, the system must be in Transaction Created.
After Prepare Signing Data completes, the system must transition to Nine-Element Hash Ready with all state invariants preserved.
Before Sign with Private Key can execute, the system must be in Nine-Element Hash Ready.
After Sign with Private Key completes, Compute v Parameter must proceed as specified by: Compute v from signature.
After Compute v Parameter completes, the system must transition to Transaction Signed with all state invariants preserved.

All data received via Receive transaction for validation from EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER-RPC must be validated before processing. Blob-specific validation required: (1) blob gas within protocol limit, (2) max_fee_per_blob_gas >= current blob base fee, (3) versioned hash has correct 0x01 prefix and 32-byte length with valid KZG correspondence, (4) blob data actually present, (5) contract creation prohibited for Type 3.
If input from EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER-RPC via Receive transaction for validation fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Extract v Parameter can execute, the system must be in Signed Transaction Received.
After Extract v Parameter completes, Check v Format must proceed as specified by: Determine format from v.
After Check v Format completes, the system must transition to Legacy Format Detected with all state invariants preserved.
After Check v Format completes, the system must transition to EIP-155 Format Detected with all state invariants preserved.
Before Extract Chain ID from v can execute, the system must be in EIP-155 Format Detected.
After Extract Chain ID from v completes, Verify Chain ID Matches Network must proceed as specified by: Verify against network.
After Verify Chain ID Matches Network completes, the system must transition to Chain ID Mismatch with all state invariants preserved.
After Verify Chain ID Matches Network completes, Recover Public Key must proceed as specified by: Chain ID matches.
Before Recover Public Key can execute, the system must be in Legacy Format Detected.
After Recover Public Key completes, the system must transition to Signature Valid with all state invariants preserved.
Data from external entity EXT-ATTACKER via Attacker captures transaction from chain A must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Attempt Replay on Chain B can execute, the system must be in Transaction on Chain A.
After Attempt Replay on Chain B completes, Validate on Chain B must proceed as specified by: Chain B processes transaction.
After Validate on Chain B completes, the system must transition to Chain ID Invalid for Network with all state invariants preserved.
After Chain ID Invalid for Network completes, Replay Attack Rejected must proceed as specified by: Reject replayed transaction.
After Validate on Chain B completes, the system must transition to Legacy TX Could Be Replayed with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP155-01): The specification uses 'SHOULD' rather than 'MUST' for the nine-element hashing, leaving room for non-compliance. — the system must enforce: Treat 'SHOULD' as mandatory for security purposes; non-compliant implementations are vulnerable to replay attacks.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP155-02): The handling of transactions with v values that don't fit the expected patterns (27, 28, or CHAIN_ID*2+35/36) is not specified. — the system must enforce: Assume transactions with invalid v values are rejected as malformed.
Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP155-03): No specification for how to handle CHAIN_ID=0 which would produce v values of 35/36. — the system must enforce: Assume CHAIN_ID=0 is invalid and should not be used.
The system assumes: Each Ethereum-compatible chain uses a unique CHAIN_ID value.. If violated: Two chains with the same CHAIN_ID would allow replay attacks between them.
The system assumes: Wallets and signing tools will correctly implement the chain ID inclusion in signatures.. If violated: Users may unknowingly create replay-vulnerable transactions.
The system assumes: Legacy transactions (v=27/28) are still accepted for backward compatibility.. If violated: Old unsigned transactions would become invalid, breaking historical compatibility.

The system assumes: Attackers can observe and rebroadcast transactions on any public chain.. If violated: If transaction visibility is limited, replay attacks become less practical (but EIP-155 still provides defense in depth).

All data received via Begin ABI validation from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P must be validated before processing. Full block validation required: header fields, gas limit bounds, PoW/PoS validity, transaction execution correctness, state root verification. All data from peers is potentially malicious.
If input from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P via Begin ABI validation fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Invoke eth_sendTransactionToContractFunction can execute, the system must be in Transaction Parameters Prepared.
After Invoke eth_sendTransactionToContractFunction completes, the system must transition to Wallet Received Transaction Request with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate ABI Matches Data completes, the system must transition to ABI Signature Validated with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate ABI Matches Data completes, the system must transition to ABI Mismatch Detected with all state invariants preserved.
Before Display Human-Readable Confirmation can execute, the system must be in ABI Signature Validated.
After Display Human-Readable Confirmation completes, the system must transition to Awaiting User Approval with all state invariants preserved.
Before Parse Function ABI can execute, the system must be in ABI Parameter Received.
After Parse Function ABI completes, Compute Function Selector must proceed as specified by: Function signature extracted.
After Compute Function Selector completes, Extract Selector from Data must proceed as specified by: Parallel extraction from data.
After Extract Selector from Data completes, Compare Function Selectors must proceed as specified by: Both selectors available.
After Compare Function Selectors completes, the system must transition to Selectors Match with all state invariants preserved.
After Compare Function Selectors completes, the system must transition to Selectors Do Not Match with all state invariants preserved.
Data from external entity EXT-DAPP via DApp supplies ABI must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Display ABI Information can execute, the system must be in Untrusted ABI from DApp.
After Display ABI Information completes, the system must transition to User Views Function Details with all state invariants preserved.
Before User Makes Trust Decision can execute, the system must be in User Views Function Details.
After User Makes Trust Decision completes, the system must transition to User Approved Transaction with all state invariants preserved.
After User Makes Trust Decision completes, the system must transition to User Rejected Transaction with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2566-01): No specification for what happens when ABI validation fails (selector mismatch) — the system must enforce: Assume wallet should reject the RPC request and return an error, or display a warning to the user about the mismatch.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2566-02): The specification says displaying function details 'is not a guarantee that a function will execute as the user expects' — the system must enforce: Assume this means the ABI could be for a different contract with the same function signature, or the contract could behave differently than the ABI suggests.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2566-03): No specification for handling ABI parsing errors or malformed ABI JSON — the system must enforce: Assume wallet should reject requests with invalid ABI JSON and return an appropriate error code.

The system assumes: Users understand that the displayed function information comes from the DApp, not from verifying the actual contract code. If violated: Users may approve transactions believing the displayed function is accurate when the contract could execute entirely different logic

The system assumes: The ABI provided by the DApp accurately represents the contract function being called. If violated: Function selector collision attacks possible - different function with same 4-byte selector could be displayed misleadingly

The system assumes: Wallets implementing this EIP will properly validate the ABI-to-data signature match. If violated: Wallets could display arbitrary function information unrelated to the actual transaction, enabling phishing attacks
Before Compute Keccak256 Hash can execute, the system must be in Bloom Filter Empty/Partial.
After Compute Keccak256 Hash completes, the system must transition to Hash Digest Available with all state invariants preserved.
Before Extract 3 Bit Positions can execute, the system must be in Hash Digest Available.
After Extract 3 Bit Positions completes, the system must transition to Bit Positions Calculated with all state invariants preserved.
Before Set Bits in Filter can execute, the system must be in Bit Positions Calculated.
After Set Bits in Filter completes, the system must transition to Bloom Filter Updated with all state invariants preserved.
Data from external entity EXT-TX-EXECUTOR via Transaction execution produces logs must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Initialize Empty Bloom can execute, the system must be in Transaction Logs Available.
After Initialize Empty Bloom completes, the system must transition to Empty Bloom Ready with all state invariants preserved.
Before Iterate Over Logs can execute, the system must be in Empty Bloom Ready.
After Iterate Over Logs completes, Add Log Address to Bloom must proceed as specified by: Process log address.
After Add Log Address to Bloom completes, Add Log Topics to Bloom must proceed as specified by: Process log topics.
After Add Log Topics to Bloom completes, the system must transition to Log Entry Processed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Iterate Over Logs can execute, the system must be in Log Entry Processed.
After Log Entry Processed completes, Logs Bloom Complete must proceed as specified by: No more logs.
Data from external entity EXT-CLIENT via Client sends log query via RPC must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Compute Query Bloom Pattern can execute, the system must be in Log Query Received.
After Compute Query Bloom Pattern completes, the system must transition to Query Pattern Computed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Bloom Filter Match can execute, the system must be in Query Pattern Computed.
After Check Bloom Filter Match completes, the system must transition to Bloom Filter Matches with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Bloom Filter Match completes, the system must transition to Bloom Filter No Match with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-BLOOM-01): The specification states 'least significant 11 bits from the first 3 16-bit words' but the endianness of word interpretation is not explicitly stated. — the system must enforce: Assume big-endian byte interpretation consistent with Ethereum's general big-endian conventions for hashes. Bytes at indices (0,1), (2,3), (4,5) form the 16-bit words.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-BLOOM-02): The false positive rate of the bloom filter is not documented. — the system must enforce: Assume standard bloom filter false positive behavior. With 2048 bits and 3 hash functions per entry, false positive rate increases with number of entries. This is a tradeoff inherent to bloom filters.

The system assumes: The keccak256 hash function is assumed to provide sufficiently uniform distribution for bloom filter bit positions.. If violated: Non-uniform hash distribution could cause bloom filter clustering, increasing false positive rates and degrading log query performance.

The system assumes: The bloom filter assumes log addresses and topics are valid 20-byte and 32-byte values respectively.. If violated: Malformed input data could produce unexpected bloom patterns, though the hash function would still process any byte sequence.

The system assumes: Clients using bloom filters for log queries must perform full log verification after bloom pre-filtering due to false positives.. If violated: Relying solely on bloom filter matches without verification could return incorrect query results.
